subject: Re: HeliosAI — Hosted->Dedicated rightsizing & QA cutover timeline
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@helios.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@helios.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted->Dedicated migration: initial sizing data and constraints

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profiles. We're ready to start scoping a Dedicated migration for our inference fleet (customer-facing chat + analytics pipelines). Before we sign the SOW we need a Redwood-verified sizing pass and a cutover timeline that fits our compliance QA window (target week of May 10).

Quick context: currently on hosted API, ~480k tokens/day, peak 240 requests/min at 99th pct, average generation length 120 tokens. We have a 2-model routing: conv-chat (longer contexts) + short-query reranker. Data residency: US-only.

Can you run an initial capacity validation and propose an acceptance / staging cutover plan? Also attach any network / peering checklists we should run with infra.

Appreciate it —
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
HeliosAI

--
Attachment: helios_sample_apicalls.json (referenced)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@helios.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: initial sizing data and constraints

Hi Tom — great, thanks for the numbers. I've looped in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (infra) to validate assumptions. High-level next steps below and a request for two quick artifacts we need to finalize sizing:

1) You: provide 72h production traces (timestamps, request_size, model routed, latency).
2) You: confirm expected QPS growth for 6 months and any peak-day events.
3) Redwood: run a workload rightsizing pass and deliver a Dedicated capacity proposal + acceptance checklist (staging runbook, smoke tests, rollback criteria).

Preliminary notes from the numbers you sent:
- 240 RPM peak => ~4 rps sustained peaks; concurrency distribution suggests modest tail.
- Models: conv-chat needs longer KV cache + larger KV size; reranker is short but latency-sensitive.
- Rough initial sizing (conservative): 2 x A40-class nodes (or equivalent T4x2 quantized profile) for baseline, scale to 3 nodes for headroom and canary.

I'll attach our sizing workbook and network checklist — fill any gaps and we'll iterate. Proposed timeline: rightsizing + validation by Apr 16, staging cutover Apr 26 - May 3, production cutover May 11 (targeting your QA window week).

Are there any hard SLAs/uptime commitments we should pre-agree for the first 90 days?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Attachment: helios-sizing-v1.xlsx (Redwood initial workbook)
Attachment: network-egress-checklist.pdf (Redwood network checks)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: initial sizing data and constraints

Rishi — internal sizing notes / questions (quick bullets):

- The "2 x A40" call from product is a good starting point but depends on quantization profile. If they can accept int8 q8_0 for reranker, that model will compress 2.5x and drop memory significantly.
- Need their 72h traces to compute realistic batching gains. Without traces we have to assume conservative batch size 4 and gpt-style attention cost.
- Network: confirm public IPs and whether traffic will egress to their analytics cluster in us-west-2; if so we need to size cross-AZ bandwidth and check MTU.
- Staging: propose 48h soak in Dedicated staging with synthetic traffic + two marker prompts for eval regressions; acceptance if 99th latency delta < 20% vs hosted baseline and no functional regressions.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the staging smoke tests and a minimal eval set (3 prompts per critical intent). Karthik — can you validate whether the A40 equivalent + nvlink pool meets our KV staging expectations?

Marissa
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: initial sizing data and constraints

Quick infra check — my read after looking at their sample request shapes:

- Peak 240 RPM with avg gen 120 tokens -> token rate ~28.8k tokens/min at peak. With batched decoding and KV caching, we can reduce per-token cost significantly.
- For conv-chat: need at least 48GB GPU memory effective after quantization for comfortable KV growth; that maps to 2 x A40 or 3 x T4xlarge (quantized) depending on the model family.
- Network: recommend a dedicated peering/VPC endpoint and an MTU test; latency target within AZ < 2ms.
- Autoscale policy: ramp from baseline 2 nodes to 4 nodes for 95th percentile sustained > 3k tokens/min over 5 minutes.

I'll draft exact CPU/GPU sizing numbers and an acceptance checklist for staging. If they can commit to the two-week validation window, we can have DR/rollback scripts ready and a canary fallback to hosted if needed.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@helios.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 8 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: initial sizing data and constraints

Tom — thanks for the fast responses and the trace files you dropped into the Drive (saw them there). Consolidated plan and timeline below — please confirm or flag changes: 

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Apr 8–12: Redwood performs rightsizing run using 72h traces, returns final node-type recommendation + cost delta and quantization options.
- Apr 13–16: Customer completes peering & MTU checks (network-egress-checklist.pdf). Redwood validates connectivity in staging.
- Apr 19–23: Redwood provisions Dedicated staging cluster (2 baseline nodes + 1 canary), runs 48h soak with synthetic & replayed traffic, executes eval prompts.
- Apr 26–May 3: Customer QA window — smoke tests + 72h acceptance; rollback criteria exercised.
- May 11: Production cutover (planned low-traffic maintenance window). Canary live for 2 hours, then progressive traffic switch.

Acceptance criteria summary:
- 99th request latency delta vs hosted <= 20%
- No functional regressions on eval prompt set (suite attached in Drive)
- Successful rollback path validated in staging

Deliverables attached / referenced:
- helios-sizing-v1.xlsx (finalized after our rightsizing)
- network-egress-checklist.pdf
- Drive link with eval prompts / tracing: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helio-rightsize
- HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HLX-DEAL-2027-042

If that timeline looks good I'll send an updated SOW (DocuSign) with the final node selection and a 90-day post-cutover monitoring bundle (included in the deal).

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@helios.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@helios.ai, maria.ortega@heliosproc.com
Date: Fri, 8 Apr 2027 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HeliosAI — Hosted->Dedicated rightsizing & QA cutover timeline

Rishi — thanks, this looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications:

1) Can you confirm the rollback time budget (how long to flip back to hosted under heavy stateful traffic)?
2) We prefer the production cutover on May 12 instead of May 11 due to an internal freeze; can you accommodate that one-day shift?

We'll aim to finish MTU/peering by Apr 16. I'll circulate the trace export to infra.

Tom
Director, Platform Engineering — HeliosAI
